subject: FinTechCo — RTBF / deletion workflow (call follow-up)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Patel <anya@fintechco.com>
Cc: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-12T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: FinTechCo — RTBF / deletion workflow (call follow-up)

Hi Anya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed:

- Scope: FinTechCo wants a documented RTBF (right to be forgotten) workflow for user account deletion that covers primary store purge, KV/cache eviction, logs/audit trails, backups, and any cross-region replicas.
- Requirements you mentioned: purge within 30 days of request for production data, immutable backups may have a 90-day deletion window but you need a plan to surface when customer data exists there, and an audit log for deletion actions for compliance reviews.
- Questions for us: exact purge timeline for primary vs. backups, whether we support legal-hold exceptions, and how deletion appears in our audit logs (searchable IDs, requestor, timestamp).

Attached is a short draft RTBF workflow (rtbf_workflow_v1.pdf) that maps Redwood's standard flow to the items we discussed. Can you confirm the required final purge window for backups (30 vs 90 days) and whether legal-hold / litigation hold will be needed for any accounts?

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm backup purge window and legal-hold requirements (reply)
2) We will produce an engineering implementation plan and timeline (ETA 3 business days after confirmation)
3) Review & sign-off with your privacy team

Happy to schedule a quick follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Attachment: rtbf_workflow_v1.pdf (summary flow + mapping)

From: Anya Patel <anya@fintechco.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: privacy@fintechco.com
Date: 2026-05-12T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinTechCo — RTBF / deletion workflow (call follow-up)

Thanks Camila — that summary looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Primary purge: must be complete within 30 days of request.
- Backups: acceptable max window is 90 days, but we need a documented process to locate and proactively delete affected customers from backups once identified.
- Logs/audit: we need tamper-evident entries that show requestor, request id, affected user ids, and deletion action time. Exportable to CSV/PDF on request.
- Legal hold: possible for a small subset of enterprise customers; we need the ability to flag an account to bypass deletion until hold is removed.

Can your engineering plan include: (a) how backups are enumerated/queried for a customer footprint; (b) expected time to execute deletion from backups once identified; (c) the exact fields captured in deletion audit records?

If you can get a 3-day turnaround on the plan, privacy@fintechco.com will be ready to review. Also looping in our infra lead if you need to coordinate on backups.

—Anya
Anya Patel
Sr. Privacy Program Manager, FinTechCo
anya@fintechco.com

Thanks for the notes — two quick engineering questions before I draft the implementation plan:

1) Backups: do we have per-customer indexing/metadata in our cold backups to efficiently identify objects for a tenant, or will deletion require a scan/restore? I think FinTechCo needs a documented maximum duration to find and remove data from backups.
2) Logs/audit: how do we currently sign or seal audit entries to be tamper-evident? Is there a cryptographic hash chain we can point to, or do we provide append-only storage with retention?

I can draft a plan with both optimistic (metadata-indexed backups) and conservative (no indexing) timelines so they can see trade-offs. Draft ETA: 48–72 hours after Anya confirms backup purge window.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.ai

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>

Cc: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, privacy@fintechco.com
Date: 2026-05-13T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinTechCo — RTBF / deletion workflow (call follow-up)

Hi Anya / privacy team — looping Mateo & Dev from engineering. Per Mateo's note, we will include two scenarios in the plan:

A) Indexed backups (preferred): if FinTechCo's backup configuration includes per-customer metadata, our deletion job can target affected objects and complete backup purge within 7–14 days after identification.
B) Non-indexed backups: if backups require restore-and-scan, the process may be 30–90 days depending on snapshot cadence and restore window; we will document mitigation and monitoring steps.

For audit/logging, Redwood provides append-only audit trails; we will add an HMAC-based seal for deletion events and include fields: request_id, requestor, affected_user_ids, action, timestamp, and deletion_scope (primary/backups/replica). We'll include example CSV exports in the plan.

Next steps (updated):
1) Anya confirms backup purge window (you indicated 90 days is acceptable) and whether legal-hold is required for any accounts.
2) Mateo & Dev will produce the two-scenario engineering plan + timeline and sample audit records (ETA 2 business days after confirmation).
3) Privacy team review and sign-off.

I've attached the current RTBF workflow draft and our backup retention policy for context. Once you confirm, we'll post the plan to the shared drive and add the HubSpot deal note: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345.

Best,
Camila

Attachment: backup-retention-policy-2025.pdf
